purpose: W9-T02..T04: genuinely distinct follow-up corpus design targeting the layers the sealed 45 leave unmutated or under-covered (commitment gateway post-commit audit/reconstruction linkage; governance-cache stale-cache admission; persistence-reconstruction transition-item write/replay).

rules.anchor_verification: each anchor is a unique exact substring (count == 1) in services/api/src/clara_api, matching the uniqueness rule enforced by evaluation/property_assurance/mutation_overlay.py (original.count(anchor) != 1 => FreezeError govmut_overlay_anchor_not_unique).
rules.distinctness_rule: each mutant must not be a near-duplicate of any of the 45 sealed mutants (mutation_site_candidates.json) and must not overlap its guard/write/reconstruction site.
rules.execution_requirement: W9 execution requires a NEW frozen protocol version, hardened dual-model non-equivalence review, new corpus freeze + M0-M3 via evaluation.property_assurance.soict_final_runner, mutant-level paired method inference, and a new seal (see W9_PROTOCOL.md). These proposals are inputs to that protocol, not results.

candidates.invariant: post-commit reconstruction linkage: a committed decision must fail reconstruction when the transition's persisted source-snapshot digest disagrees with the linked manifest (commitment_snapshot_transition_digest_mismatch)
candidates.fault_family: reconstruction-linkage bypass (audit/reconstruction integrity; P8 digest lineage)
candidates.reason_distinct: All 45 sealed mutants leave the reconstruct_commitment_decision linkage intact. M08-C mutates a different comparison (manifest self-digest manifest_fingerprint != manifest.manifest_digest inside gateway.reconstruct_snapshot_artifact); this mutant severs the transition->manifest digest lineage that commit-time binding cannot observe. No sealed mutant touches commitment_gateway.reconstruct_commitment_decision.

candidates.invariant: bitemporal reconstruction cutoff: reconstruct_commitments must not include transitions recorded after the knowledge-time cutoff (known_at is the observation coordinate, never ingestion timing)
candidates.reason_distinct: No sealed mutant mutates a reconstruction query filter. All 45 guard/digest/idempotency mutants execute during admission/commit; this is a read-side replay fault that leaks late-arriving backdated commitment transitions into historical reconstruction.

candidates.invariant: reconstruction history completeness: reconstruct_commitments must fail (commitment_history_incomplete) when a transition's result version row is missing
candidates.reason_distinct: No sealed mutant touches the commitment_history_incomplete guard or any bulk-reconstruction completeness check. The 45 are all write/admission-side; this is a read-side completeness fault in reconstruct_commitments (bulk variant; W9-C04 is the single-decision variant at a distinct site).

candidates.invariant: reconstruction history completeness: reconstruct_commitment_decision must fail (commitment_history_incomplete) when the committed decision's result version row is missing
candidates.reason_distinct: Same fault family as W9-C03 but a distinct enforcement site (single-decision reconstruction vs bulk reconstruction), mirroring how the sealed corpus spreads one family across multiple sites. No sealed mutant covers either site.

candidates.invariant: persistence integrity: a committed transition must record an advancing resulting state version (resulting == base + 1), keeping the decision ledger consistent with the canonical GlhsStateVersion counter
candidates.fault_family: non-advancing state-version write (persistence-reconstruction; P13 state/audit atomicity)
candidates.reason_distinct: No sealed mutant alters a persisted write value of the commitment transition (M01/M02/M14 mutate guards and the idempotency key hash, not the resulting_state_version write). This mutant records a stale non-advancing resulting version while the GlhsStateVersion row still advances, so the decision ledger diverges from the canonical counter.

candidates.invariant: governance-cache freshness: a persisted snapshot manifest (the governance snapshot cache) must not be admitted without revalidation of its schema version (proposal_snapshot_schema_mismatch)
candidates.fault_family: stale governance-cache consulted for admission (P10/P12 freshness; M12 unanchored family)
candidates.reason_distinct: The sealed M08-D mutates a sibling guard in the same function (digest_algorithm), but no sealed mutant mutates the schema-version revalidation of the cached manifest. This exercises the stale-cache admission fault M12 was designed for, at an anchor that exists in current source (M12 had no one-line anchor).

candidates.invariant: governance-cache freshness: a cached snapshot manifest with a foreign canonicalization profile must not be admitted (proposal_snapshot_canonicalization_mismatch), because its digests are computed under a different canonical form
candidates.fault_family: stale governance-cache consulted for admission (P10/P12 freshness; M12 unanchored family)
candidates.reason_distinct: No sealed mutant mutates the canonicalization-profile revalidation. It is a separate guard from M08-D (digest algorithm) and M08-A/M08-B/M08-C (digest values); bypassing it admits a cache entry whose digest semantics cannot be verified, a distinct fault from skipping a digest comparison.

candidates.invariant: governance-cache scope: a cached snapshot may only be admitted for evidence that its disclosed provenance actually covers (proposal_evidence_not_disclosed)
candidates.fault_family: stale governance-cache consulted for admission / evidence-disclosure bypass (P11 provenance; M12 family)
candidates.reason_distinct: M11 family mutates evidence-row existence/scope checks (record_evidence, _assertion_evidence_ids, commitment evidence subset), never the snapshot's disclosed-provenance subset revalidation. This mutant admits a proposal whose evidence was not disclosed in the cached snapshot, which no sealed mutant can reach.

candidates.invariant: transition-item persistence: an activation must be recorded as an activate transition item so reconstruct_state replay makes the assertion visible (only action == "activate" adds to active_ids)
candidates.fault_family: transition item not recorded for replay (persistence-reconstruction; P9/P13)
candidates.reason_distinct: No sealed mutant modifies any GlhsTransitionItem write. All 45 are guard/digest/idempotency mutations; this one corrupts the persisted transition-item action so the write exists but replay silently loses the activation, a fault only observable through reconstruct_state/compile_thss.

candidates.invariant: bitemporal reconstruction cutoff: reconstruct_state must not replay transitions recorded after the knowledge-time cutoff
candidates.reason_distinct: Gateway-side counterpart of W9-C02 at a distinct site (generic reconstruct_state vs commitment reconstruct_commitments). No sealed mutant mutates a replay query filter; M13-B mutates the row.valid_to visibility predicate, not the recorded_at knowledge cutoff.

candidates.invariant: dedup reject persistence: a historical duplicate with the same asserted anchor must be rejected and that rejection persisted as a reject transition item (plus state version and outbox); bypassing it leaves both assertions active
candidates.fault_family: dedup-reject transition item not written (persistence-reconstruction; P9/P13)
candidates.reason_distinct: The sealed M13 family mutates the current-state query (lifecycle_status in_ ACTIVE) and the valid_to visibility predicate, never the same-anchor dedup-reject branch. This mutant suppresses the whole reject write path (GlhsTransitionItem reject, GlhsStateVersion, outbox), a persistence fault distinct from the M13 selection faults.
